deck_title: Archimedes-Bouguer GM = KB + I_wp/V - KG metacentric hull roll stability vs naive fixed buoyancy center rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Archimedes (c. 250 BC) & Pierre Bouguer (1746) naval hydrostatics metacentric roll stability law (waterplane second moment of area I_wp shifting the center of buoyancy laterally by BM * sin(theta) = (I_wp / V) * sin(theta) so metacentric height GM = KB + BM - KG = GM_0 * (1 + u) and righting torque tau = rho * g * V * GM * sin(theta), locking tau_exact / tau_model = 1.0000x across all 17 stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive fixed center-of-buoyancy script (ignoring waterplane wedge shift Delta_BM, which underestimates righting torque by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-strip immersed/emerged waterplane wedge quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: 3D ocean ships, wide-beam cargo barges, catamarans, floating icebergs, and buoyant crate roll-oscillation animations
Evaluating metacentric radius BM = I_wp / V = B^2 / (12 * draft) so hulls with center of gravity G above static center of buoyancy B_0 remain upright whenever M lies above G (GM > 0)
Driving natural ship roll period T_roll = 2*pi * k_xx / sqrt(g * GM)
not_for: Fully submerged submarines where waterplane area I_wp = 0 and BM = 0 (requiring B strictly above G)
